issues.title: Switching the fee recipient back on is not delayed for claims already pending: an admin can undo a cut to zero in the same block as finalizeClaim
issues.location: contracts/InheritanceVault.sol:1137-1138 (finalizeClaim fee line); compare initiateClaim :1061 and setFeeRecipient :1248-1255
issues.problem: v2 treats removing the fee recipient as a cut to zero that applies at once. Setting a recipient after a period with none is supposed to be a 'raise from zero' that waits FEE_RAISE_DELAY (feeRecipientActiveAt). Only initiateClaim applies that delay. finalizeClaim checks `feeTo == address(0)` and never checks feeRecipientActiveAt. Scenario: a claim locks 50 bps while a recipient is in force. The admin then removes the recipient, so fees are publicly off and, per the NatSpec, 'a cut during the challenge window still reaches the heir'. The admin can re-set the recipient in the same block, just before finalizeClaim (which is permissionless, so the admin can send it), and the heir is charged the full locked fee. The claimFeeBps channel does not have this hole: a re-raise after setClaimFee(0) is only scheduled and never reaches the pending claim. This breaks the FEES header guarantee at :79-80 ('no rate a user pays can be raised in the same block as, and just before, that user's transaction') and :91-92. It also contradicts setFeeRecipient's NatSpec at :1245-1247. The heir never pays more than the lockedFeeBps visible at claim start (at most the ceiling, at most 1%), so no value beyond the lock is at risk. v1 finalize has the same line, so this is an incomplete F05/F06 fix, not a newly introduced defect. CHANGELOG-v2.md:239-243 closes this sandwich one step earlier, at initiateClaim, but not at settlement.
issues.evidence: Sandbox poc/REV1-regression, test/rev1-fee-recipient.ts (contracts/InheritanceVault.sol there is byte-identical to the repo; checked with diff -q). Command: `cd .../poc/REV1-regression && npx hardhat test test/rev1-fee-recipient.ts` gives 1 passing, 1 failing. The control passes: a cut to 0 via setClaimFee followed by setClaimFee(50) in the same block as finalizeClaim leaves feeSink credit 0. The failing test: setFeeRecipient(0) mid-window, then in one block setFeeRecipient(feeSink) [higher tip] and finalizeClaim. It asserts feeRecipientActiveAt() > block time (the contract itself says the recipient is not in force), yet `fee re-imposed by a recipient switched on in the settlement block: expected 0, actual 500000000000000000` (50 bps of 100 ETH). The code at :1138 is `uint256 fee = feeTo == address(0) ? 0 : (amt * bps) / BPS_DENOMINATOR;`. In initiateClaim :1061 the check is `if (feeRecipient != address(0) && block.timestamp >= feeRecipientActiveAt)`.
issues.fix: In finalizeClaim, treat a recipient that is not yet in force as no recipient: `uint256 fee = feeTo == address(0) || block.timestamp < feeRecipientActiveAt ? 0 : (amt * bps) / BPS_DENOMINATOR;`. Verified in the sandbox (patched copy saved as poc/REV1-regression/InheritanceVault.sol.fixed): the PoC passes and AuditPrelim2026-09 + Audit + InheritanceVault + rev1 give 185 passing, 0 failing. Runtime size 20,338 bytes (+21). Add the failing test above to the F05 block in test/AuditPrelim2026-09.ts. It fails on v2 as written and on v1 (v1 has no delay at all).

issues.title: F09 partially closed: the payee rule is address-based, so a non-canonical wrap-and-return contract or a SELFDESTRUCT bounce still turns a credited payout into admin-sweepable surplus
issues.location: contracts/InheritanceVault.sol:639-642 _checkPayee, :650-663 _payout (NATIVE branch), :1284-1291 sweepSurplus; guarantee at :53-56 (T4) and :106-111 (PAYOUT ADDRESSES)
issues.problem: v2 refuses only address(this), the immutable wrappedNative and listed tokens as a payee. The F09 mechanism is really about the class: a native payout to a contract that sends value back to msg.sender, i.e. the vault. Any contract whose receive() wraps the coin and forwards a LISTED token to the sender, or bounces the coin back with SELFDESTRUCT, is still accepted as the initiateClaim recipient, the withdraw `to` and the withdrawCredit `to`. After PUSH_GRACE anyone pushes; the credit is retired and the value lands outside every lane (WETH surplus, or native surplus), and sweepSurplus hands it to the admin. This is narrower than the original F09, which needed the canonical WETH address. But it is the same impact, and it breaks the T4 claim that the admin cannot reach 'any credited payout. That is arithmetic'.
issues.evidence: Failing tests in C:/Users/Vinoth/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Vinoth-OneDrive-Claude-claude-code/005aaa32-3c49-4f96-8428-bacda0a96f78/scratchpad/poc/REV1-closure/test/poc-REV1-closure.ts (mocks WrapAndReturnGateway and SelfdestructBouncer in contracts/test/Rev1Closure.sol). The deployment is Base-like: WETH is both wrappedNative and listed. Run: `npx hardhat test test/poc-REV1-closure.ts`. Output: "credited to heir's payee: 9950000000000000000; surplus(WETH) after push: 9950000000000000000; admin swept: 9950000000000000000" -> AssertionError 'the admin swept the heir's credited payout' (expected 0). "credited: 9950000000000000000; surplus(NATIVE) after push: 9950000000000000000" -> AssertionError. Code: InheritanceVault.sol:641 `if (isSupportedToken[to] || (to == wrappedNative && to != NATIVE)) revert ForbiddenPayoutAddress(to);` is the only payee test. :53 'The admin cannot reach a wei of any vault's balance or any credited payout.'
issues.fix: Preferred, class-level and cheap because the list is immutable and short: in _payout's NATIVE branch, snapshot address(this).balance and balanceOf(this) for each _supportedTokens entry before the call. After it, require address(this).balance == before - amount and every listed balance unchanged, otherwise revert, and the credit is kept. That is at most about 5 staticcalls, and only on native payouts. If bytecode or gas rules this out, scope T4 and PAYOUT ADDRESSES instead: a payout to a contract that sends value back to this contract (a wrap-and-forward helper, a SELFDESTRUCT bounce) becomes sweepable surplus. The APP disposition should also warn on any payee with code, not only on the known WETH and token addresses.

issues.title: F33 partially closed: totalLocked/totalCredited public getters still expose the half-applied deposit, contrary to the VIEWS NatSpec
issues.location: contracts/InheritanceVault.sol:300-301 (public mappings totalLocked/totalCredited), :622-635 _pull called before the lanes are written in createVault :698/:720 and topUp :748/:754; NatSpec :132-136
issues.problem: The plan's four views (surplus, getVault, getOpenVaults, creditOf) now revert mid-transaction. But the public mapping getters totalLocked and totalCredited cannot take the modifier, and still answer inside a token callback. A proof-of-reserve integrator computes balanceOf(vault) - totalLocked - totalCredited, which is exactly what surplus() does. Inside the deposit window it therefore still reads a phantom surplus equal to the in-flight deposit, which is the original F33 symptom. The header now claims 'code called back from inside such a call can never read a half-applied state', which is false. This follows the plan literally (the REACH-FIX suggested making these internal with guarded getters), so it is a partial closure plus an inaccurate NatSpec claim, not a fund risk.
issues.evidence: Failing test 'a token callback inside the deposit window reads a phantom surplus from totalLocked/totalCredited' in .../poc/REV1-closure/test/poc-REV1-closure.ts (mock LaneProbeToken). Output: "lanesOk=true balance=150000000000000000000 locked=100000000000000000000 credited=0 => phantom surplus 50000000000000000000". surplusOk is false, so the guard works on surplus(). The failure is AssertionError 'totalLocked/totalCredited expose the half-applied deposit'. NatSpec InheritanceVault.sol:134: 'or calls out -- so code called back from inside such a call can never read a half-applied'.
issues.fix: Either make totalLocked and totalCredited internal and add `function totalLocked(address) external view nonReentrantView` and `totalCredited(address)` getters with the same names and selectors, so the ABI is unchanged (the F33 REACH-FIX). Or narrow the NatSpec to the four guarded views, and state that the public lane getters show pre-deposit lanes against the post-transfer balance while a deposit is in flight.

issues.title: F15 residual: an all-skipped checkInMany reverts a bare NothingCheckedIn(), so for a one-vault owner a running claim is indistinguishable from a harmless no-op
issues.location: contracts/InheritanceVault.sol:793-825 checkInMany (:824 `if (refreshed == 0) revert NothingCheckedIn();`), :435 error NothingCheckedIn(), NatSpec :786-791
issues.problem: The success masquerade is closed: a mined batch logs CheckedIn or CheckInSkipped for every id. When no id moves, though, the batch reverts, so the CheckInSkipped logs are rolled back and the error carries no reason. For the most common keeper (one owner, one vault), 'claim pending' (SKIP_CLAIM_PENDING, the case F15 exists for) returns the same revert data as an unknown id, an id already moved in this block (SKIP_REPEATED, see the existing test at AuditPrelim2026-09.ts:2161) or a pinned vault. A keeper that treats NothingCheckedIn as 'already done, retry later' misses the claim. The NatSpec 'every id in the call gets exactly one log' does not hold on that path.
issues.evidence: Failing test 'a one-vault keeper cannot tell ...' in .../poc/REV1-closure/test/poc-REV1-closure.ts. Output: "claim pending -> 0x0a2ce31a; unknown id -> 0x0a2ce31a" (0x0a2ce31a = keccak('NothingCheckedIn()')[:4], verified), followed by AssertionError 'the revert must say a claim is pending'.
issues.fix: Carry the reasons in the error, for example `error NothingCheckedIn(uint256 firstId, uint8 firstReason)` or a bitmask of the SKIP_* reasons seen. Then a one-vault batch with a pending claim reverts with SKIP_CLAIM_PENDING visible in the revert data. Keeper docs and the APP should also treat any NothingCheckedIn as 'read getVault now', never as a harmless duplicate.

issues.title: F20 side effect: beneficiaryCancelClaim lets a stolen heir key redirect a pending payout; the NatSpec says it gives nobody new power
issues.location: contracts/InheritanceVault.sol:1074-1098 beneficiaryCancelClaim and its NatSpec (:1080)
issues.problem: In v1 the claim recipient is frozen at initiateClaim, so an heir key compromised during the challenge window cannot move the payout. The F20 severity reviewer called this the frozen-recipient protection and suggested keeping it with a short re-point grace. The plan chose an unrestricted cancel. Now the beneficiary key alone can cancel and re-initiate to any address until finalizeClaim is mined. With the owner gone, which is the product's main case, a heir key phished on day 13 of a 14-day window redirects the whole estate, at the cost of one more window. This is a deliberate plan trade-off, not a broken fix. But the NatSpec claim is inaccurate, and neither the heir docs nor the APP disclose it.
issues.evidence: Failing test 'once a claim is pending, the beneficiary key alone cannot redirect the payout' in .../poc/REV1-closure/test/poc-REV1-closure.ts. Output: "credited to the address chosen after the key was stolen: 10000000000000000000", followed by AssertionError 'the payout fixed at claim start was redirected by the beneficiary key'. NatSpec InheritanceVault.sol:1080: 'It gives nobody new power over the funds.' digest F20 SEV-FIX: 'It also keeps the frozen-recipient protection: a thief who steals the heir key after initiation still cannot redirect the payout.'
issues.fix: A lead decision is needed. Either (a) limit the cancel to a short grace after claimInitiatedAt (for example 24-72 h), which is enough to fix a typo but closes the late-theft window; or (b) keep it, correct the NatSpec to say a compromised beneficiary key can redirect a pending payout until finalization, and tell heirs in the docs and APP to finalize promptly and to treat the heir key as hot for the whole window.

issues.title: F38 ERC777 test's 'refused before its sender hook can run' is unprovable: it reads state after a reverted tx (vacuous assertion)
issues.location: test/AuditPrelim2026-09.ts:2374-2382 (also :229 facade.lastAmount and :189 dbl.balanceOf(admin), read after a reverted sweep)
issues.problem: The test asserts hookCalls is unchanged after dep.deposit reverts with UnsupportedToken. A revert rolls back every state change made inside it, including the hook's hookCalls += 1, so this assertion cannot fail whether or not the vault called the token before refusing it. The title's ordering claim is therefore untested. The same self-confirming pattern appears in F01, where facade.lastAmount and the admin's dbl balance are read after a reverted sweep. There the revertedWithCustomError assertion carries the test, but the comments present these values as independent measurements.
issues.evidence: Mutant M40 moves `if (!isSupportedToken[token]) revert UnsupportedToken(token);` in _pull to AFTER safeTransferFrom and the second balanceOf, so an unlisted token IS called (and its hook runs) before the refusal. Result: 'M40 SURVIVED pass=183 fail=0', and the F38 hook test still passes (poc/REV1-tests-mut/mutants-result.txt, batch2).
issues.fix: Make the ordering observable without relying on post-revert state. For example, arm the unlisted HookToken (or give it a transferFrom) so that it reverts with its own distinctive reason when called, then assert the revert is UnsupportedToken, which can only happen if the vault refused it before the call. Drop or relabel the post-revert state reads (hookCalls, lastAmount, the admin balance), or say in a comment that they only restate the revert.

issues.title: Round-1 fix #2 (_holdings) lets any listed token freeze every NATIVE payout: a returndata bomb or gas-burning balanceOf defeats the 'reads as max' tolerance
issues.location: contracts/InheritanceVault.sol:701-711 (_holdings loop, lines 705-709); called from _payout at 683 and 686; false NatSpec at 697-700
issues.problem: Round 1 made every native payout read balanceOf on every listed token, twice. The read uses a Solidity low-level staticcall, which forwards 63/64 of the remaining gas and copies the WHOLE returndata into memory. The tolerance ('A balanceOf that fails reads as type(uint256).max ... so a listed token that stops answering cannot also freeze native payouts') holds only for a token that reverts cheaply. A listed token whose balanceOf returns a returndata bomb, or burns the gas it is given, makes every native withdrawCredit, pushCredit and sweepSurplus(NATIVE) run out of gas at ANY gas limit up to the 16,777,216 transaction cap. The bomb's callee gets 63x the gas the caller keeps, so the caller can never afford to copy the returndata. v1 had no cross-asset dependency: a native payout read no token. This is issuer-level (or compromised-upgrade-key, or buggy-upgrade) exposure. On the proposed lists, Base USDC, EURC and cbBTC and BNB USDC are upgradeable proxies. So one listed issuer can now freeze every ETH/BNB heir's inheritance, every owner's native withdrawal, and the native sweep. Nothing is lost: the credit is intact and pays once the token behaves (control test). But it is a new denial of service on assets the token has nothing to do with, and it contradicts the fix's own NatSpec.

issues.title: wrappedNative is not required to be a listed token, so a wrap-and-return payee silently turns a native payout into stranded wrapped coin (no PayoutReturned)
issues.location: contracts/InheritanceVault.sol:499-525 (constructor accepts any wrappedNative_); _holdings 701-711 measures only _supportedTokens; scripts/deploy.ts tokenConfig() has the same gap under the SUPPORTED_TOKENS/WRAPPED_NATIVE overrides
issues.problem: PAYOUT ADDRESSES says the wrap-on-receive rule is 'enforced by measurement': a native payout that sends value back reverts PayoutReturned and the credit stays, so the account can pick another destination. The measurement covers only listed tokens. The constructor accepts a wrappedNative_ that is not in `supported`, and the deploy script's overrides can produce one. In that configuration, withdrawCredit(NATIVE, helper) through a wrap-and-forward helper succeeds. The credit is retired, and the returned WETH sits in the vault outside every lane. sweepSurplus refuses it (UnsupportedToken), so it is stranded for good. T4 still holds, since the admin gains nothing. But the account loses the payout, where a listed WETH would have reverted and let it retry. The proposed tables list WETH/WBNB on every network, so the default deploys are not affected.
issues.fix: In the constructor, add: if (wrappedNative_ != address(0) && !isSupportedToken[wrappedNative_]) revert InvalidTokenConfig(wrappedNative_). This also puts it in _holdings. Alternatively, include wrappedNative in the _holdings digest even when it is unlisted. Mirror the check in scripts/deploy.ts before sending.

issues.title: beneficiaryCancelClaim is not atomic with re-initiation: the ACTIVE gap re-opens powers the pending claim had shut (past the horizon the owner can re-point the heir at once; before it, any holder of a chain value can push the heir back a full period)
issues.location: contracts/InheritanceVault.sol:1151-1159 (beneficiaryCancelClaim) and its NatSpec 1127-1150
issues.problem:
The F20 remedy for a mistyped recipient is cancel, then re-initiate: two transactions, with the vault ACTIVE in between. ClaimCancelled announces the gap publicly. In the gap, everything a pending claim blocks works again:

(a) Past the horizon, setBeneficiary and setInactivityPeriod revert HorizonReached while the claim is pending. After the cancel they succeed. The owner can re-point the heir with no cooldown, and the new heir claims at once, because the deadline is clamped to the past horizon. Doing the same through extendHorizon would cost a full inactivity period.

(b) Before the horizon, checkInByChain reverts VaultNotActive while the claim is pending. After the cancel, anyone holding an unspent chain value (a bearer credential, F17) or the owner's check-in automation can check in. That pushes the heir's re-initiate back a whole inactivity period (NotYetExpired).

The NatSpec mentions only that the owner or a chain relayer 'may check in'. It says nothing on (a), and it does not say that the relayer is anyone holding a value. issues.title: The round-1 F09 fix lets the issuer of any listed ERC20 freeze every native payout and native sweep
issues.location: contracts/InheritanceVault.sol: _payout native branch (lines 682-686) and _holdings (lines 701-711); the NatSpec above _holdings (697-700) and CHANGELOG-v2.md Review round 1, item 2
issues.problem: Review round 1 made every native payout (withdrawCredit, pushCredit, sweepSurplus(NATIVE)) read balanceOf(vault) twice on every listed token and compare the two readings. A native payout therefore depends on how each listed ERC20 answers. v1 native payouts call no ERC20 at all. An issuer upgrade of any listed token breaks the comparison for every payee, including plain EOA heirs. Four listed tokens are upgradeable proxies: Base USDC, EURC and cbBTC, and BNB USDC (pass 4 records this). Three upgraded behaviours freeze the lane. First, a returndata bomb: the vault copies the whole return with `bytes memory ret`, and the callee holds 63/64 of the gas, so it can always return more data than the caller can afford to copy. Second, a balanceOf that burns all its gas. Third, a balanceOf that answers differently on its two reads, which gives PayoutReturned. The code handles only a balanceOf that reverts. So an issuer action on USDC can lock heirs who chose native coin precisely to avoid issuer risk. F12 accepts issuer risk only for that token's own vaults. The NatSpec says 'a listed token that stops answering cannot also freeze native payouts', and round 1 says 'the new revert lets a payee grief only its own payout'. Both claims are false as written.
issues.evidence: Sandbox scratchpad/poc/REV2-closure. The mock is contracts/rev2/Rev2Tokens.sol (Rev2IssuerToken, whose setMode stands in for a proxy upgade). The test is test/poc-REV2-closure.ts. Setup: a native estate settled to heir bob (an EOA), with IUSD listed next to WETH and a plain token. `npx hardhat test test/poc-REV2-closure.ts` on the current v2 source (byte-identical to the repo, checked with diff) gives 4 failing: '[v2] heir withdrawCredit(NATIVE) with 16777216 gas: FAILED: Transaction ran out of gas' (mode 2, bomb); "owner withdrawCredit(NATIVE) under mode 3: FAILED: ... reverted with custom error 'PayoutReturned(0x7099...79C8)'"; 'mode 4 at 16777216 gas: FAILED: Transaction ran out of gas'; 'sweepSurplus(NATIVE) under mode 2: FAILED: Transaction ran out of gas'. 16,777,216 is the most gas any transaction may use: hardhat refuses 29M with 'exceeds transaction gas cap of 16777216'. The unrelated plain-token lane still pays, so the freeze is native-specific. Contract payees fail in modes 2, 3 and 4 as well (the logging test). The control passes: mode 0 pays, and mode 1 (revert) is handled. `VAULT_IMPL=v1 npx hardhat test test/poc-REV2-closure.ts` gives 5 passing ('[v1] ... paid' in every mode).
issues.fix: 1. In _payout's native branch, measure only when the payee has code: `bool measured = to.code.length != 0;`. Take _holdings before and compare after only if measured. A codeless payee runs nothing during the call, so it cannot send value back. A 7702-delegated EOA has code and stays measured. 2. In _holdings, read each balance with an assembly staticcall capped at a fixed amount of gas (for example 50,000) that copies at most 32 bytes: `staticcall(50000, t, ptr, 36, ptr, 32)`, with a success-and-returndatasize>=32 check and type(uint256).max otherwise. This removes the bomb and the gas-burn cases. 3. Correct the NatSpec (T4, PAYOUT ADDRESSES, _holdings) and the changelog. The residual to disclose: a listed token that answers balanceOf inconsistently within one transaction can still block native payouts to CONTRACT payees. Those payees can route through withdrawCredit(NATIVE, eoa). I trial-applied 1+2 in the sandbox (trialfix.js) and then restored the source. With the fix, all 211 existing tests pass, all 5 PoC tests pass, and a contract payee is paid under modes 2 and 4 (mode 3 still gives PayoutReturned, as disclosed). issues.problem: The F18 text says that in the last inactivity period before the horizon a chain check-in reverts DeadlinePinnedAtHorizon and keeps the value unspent. The doc adds "Check-ins stop at the horizon, and in v2 one period earlier." The code only reverts once the stored deadline already equals the horizon. The first check-in inside the last period still moves the deadline (clamped to the horizon, up to almost a full period later) and spends a value. Only the check-ins after it revert. The chain feature exists for a keyless owner. A relayer that follows the text and stops at horizon minus one period leaves the deadline short of the horizon, so the heir can claim up to nearly one period earlier than the chain could have prevented. The contract logic is correct: the generator (scripts/checkin-chain.ts:297, `deadline >= absoluteDeadline`) and checkIn's own comment (:865-867) describe it correctly. Only the prose is wrong.

The companion test passes: CheckedIn(alice, 0, horizon, true), the deadline moves to the horizon (more than 14 days of extra liveness), hbLeft goes from 3 to 2 (a value was spent), and only the next value reverts DeadlinePinnedAtHorizon. issues.title: F15 partially closed: past the horizon, a pending claim is reported as SKIP_CLAIM_PENDING, whose documented remedy (abortClaim) reverts HorizonReached
issues.location: contracts/InheritanceVault.sol:205-206 (SKIP_CLAIM_PENDING NatSpec), :909-911 (checkInMany tests claim state before the horizon), :859 (checkIn reverts ClaimPendingUseAbort before its horizon check), :1230 (abortClaim reverts HorizonReached)
issues.problem: The F15 reason codes are meant to name the remedy ("why checkInMany did not refresh an id, and so what fixes it"). Suppose a vault is past its horizon with a claim pending. checkInMany then logs CheckInSkipped(reason 3), or reverts NothingCheckedIn(8) for a one-vault batch. That is byte-identical to a pending claim before the horizon. The constant's NatSpec says the fix is abortClaim, and at or after the horizon abortClaim always reverts HorizonReached. There, only extendHorizon (to at least now + inactivityPeriod) or a full withdrawal stops the claim. A v2 keeper or app that maps the reason to its documented remedy sends a Veto that fails, while a challenge window of as little as 7 days runs out. This is the F03/F19 trap, reintroduced through the new API. checkIn's ClaimPendingUseAbort points the same wrong way past the horizon (inherited from v1).

Sandbox scratchpad/poc/REV3-closure/test/poc-REV3-closure.ts. Command: cd scratchpad/poc/REV3-closure && npx hardhat test test/poc-REV3-closure.ts. Failing tests (log in scratchpad/poc/REV3-closure/poc-run.log):

The receipt gives [[1, 3]]; the output prints `SKIP_CLAIM_PENDING NatSpec: /// @dev A claim is pending. A check-in never ends one: abortClaim (the veto) does.`, `getVault: state 2, horizonReached true`, `abortClaim (the named remedy): HorizonReached`, then `AssertionError: Expected transaction NOT to be reverted` at poc-REV3-closure.ts:93.
2) "BYPASS (one-vault keeper): NothingCheckedIn(8) past the horizon ...". checkInMany([id]) reverts NothingCheckedIn(8), the same data as before the horizon, and abortClaim then reverts (poc-REV3-closure.ts:104).
Source: InheritanceVault.sol:205 `/// @dev A claim is pending. A check-in never ends one: abortClaim (the veto) does.`; :909 `if (s == STATE_CLAIM_PENDING) skip = SKIP_CLAIM_PENDING;` comes before :911 `else if (block.timestamp >= v.absoluteDeadline) skip = SKIP_HORIZON_REACHED;`.

Its NatSpec should name the real remedies: extendHorizon to at least now + inactivityPeriod, or withdraw(id, type(uint256).max, to). At minimum, scope SKIP_CLAIM_PENDING's NatSpec to "before the horizon" and say that NothingCheckedIn(8) must be read together with getVault().horizonReached. Optional and cheap: in checkIn, test the horizon before the claim state, so a past-horizon owner gets HorizonReached rather than ClaimPendingUseAbort. The F18 control that pins ClaimPendingUseAbort past the horizon would then need updating. Add a regression test in the F15 block, and have any v2 app or watcher map the reason to the remedy.

issues.title: F08 closed as specified, but a credit smaller than what the account already owes gets no grace of its own: a stranger can settle and push it in one transaction
issues.location: contracts/InheritanceVault.sol:626-631 (_credit restarts creditedSince only if amount >= owed), :1267 (finalizeClaim credits the recipient), :145-152 (THE CREDIT LANE), :1297-1302 (pushCredit @dev)
issues.problem: The push grace is kept per (token, account), not per credit. Take an heir whose payout address still holds an older credit at least PUSH_GRACE old. That can be their own first inheritance from a split estate, a lifetime gift from the owner, or a second estate from another relative. A later, smaller inheritance joins the expired clock. finalizeClaim is permissionless, so a stranger can settle that claim and push the whole balance in one transaction (the original F08 SettleAndPush attack). The new inheritance then has zero seconds of grace. The round-2 deviation argued that exposing an inheritance costs a plant "at least as large as the inheritance". That holds for attacker-funded plants, but here the heir's own stale credit is the plant, and it costs the attacker nothing. The NatSpec overstates the guarantee: "so the account always has that long to route it elsewhere first" and "a credited account that CAN act always gets to route its credit first". The header discloses the effect only for the fee recipient. The rule itself is deliberate: the suite pins "one wei smaller does not" restart.
issues.evidence: Sandbox test scratchpad/poc/REV3-closure/test/poc-REV3-closure.ts, "BYPASS: an heir's SMALLER second inheritance rides on the clock of an older credit and is settled-and-pushed in one transaction". Setup: two SenderBlocklistToken vaults (100 and 10) name bob; both claims start together; vault 0 is finalized; 30 days pass without a pull; the issuer blocklists bob. A stranger's SettleAndPush.run(vault 1) then prints `stranger settle-and-push of the second inheritance: WENT THROUGH` and `after destroyBlackFunds bob holds 0 (both inheritances)`, and the test fails with `the second inheritance had zero seconds of grace: expected true to equal false` (poc-REV3-closure.ts:153). The control in the same file, "a fresh inheritance on an account that owes nothing cannot be settled-and-pushed", passes with PushTooEarly, so the older credit is the only difference.
issues.fix: No code change recommended. Restarting on every credit, or restarting once the old clock has expired, would let a griefer postpone the push to a passive account (an exchange deposit address) indefinitely for 1 wei every 30 days, which is the cost the >= rule exists to prevent. Correct the NatSpec instead, in THE CREDIT LANE and on pushCredit. Say the grace runs per account balance: a credit smaller than what is already owed joins the older clock, and once that clock has run out it can be settled and pushed in one transaction. Add heir DOC/APP guidance: withdraw any older credit before settling another claim into the same address, or name a fresh recipient per claim (before settlement, beneficiaryCancelClaim can still change it).

issues.title: New F06 fee-schedule branches are untested at their boundaries: three mutants survive the whole suite
issues.location: contracts/InheritanceVault.sol:1362 (applyClaimFee), :651 (_recordMaturedRaise), :1346 (setClaimFee cut branch); F06 block of test/AuditPrelim2026-09.ts:1337-1402
issues.problem:
The F06 tests pin claimFeeBps() at the exact second of pendingClaimFeeAt, but not the three other new branches that share that boundary.
(T1) applyClaimFee `<` changed to `<=`: it would refuse FeeRaiseNotDue at the very second claimFeeBps() already reports the raise. The test uses time.increaseTo(at), so the call lands at at+1.
(T2) _recordMaturedRaise `>=` changed to `>`: a setClaimFee at exactly pendingClaimFeeAt would be measured from the old recorded rate. The changelog calls this rule 'a cut measured from a matured-but-unapplied raise'.
(T3) every cut emits ClaimFeeRaiseCancelled(0) even when no raise is pending, which an indexer would read as a cancelled raise.
None of these can raise a user's fee (T2 only lowers it). They are gaps in the tests of new code that the changelog describes as tested.
